tagline: Powersports innovation driving adventure and utility.
hero_kpi_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA reflects Polaris's operational performance after adjustments for exceptional charges (Indian Motorcycle divestiture, asset impairments). This metric neutralizes non-recurring impacts to better assess the operational health of the recreational vehicle portfolio.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Gross operating profit adjusted, excluding exceptional charges such as impairments and losses on divestitures.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA declined from $635.4M in 2024 to $410.2M in 2025, a 35% decrease, primarily driven by charges related to the Indian Motorcycle group divestiture and asset impairments.
kpis.signal: 35% decline year-over-year, impacted by exceptional items.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Gross margin declined from 20.4% in 2024 to 19.1% in 2025, a contraction of 130 basis points, driven by additional tariffs, elevated promotional costs, and increased incentive costs.
kpis.signal: Margin pressure due to tariffs and elevated promotional activity.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Revenue was $7.15B in 2025 ($7.152B exactly), essentially flat versus 2024 ($7.175B), representing a decline of less than 1%, following a 20% decline in 2024.
kpis.signal: Stabilization after sharp 2024 decline, with modest negative variance.

kpis.name: Net Loss
kpis.explanation: Net loss after all charges, taxes, and amortization, attributable to Polaris Inc. shareholders.
kpis.description: Net loss attributable to Polaris Inc. was $465.5M in 2025 versus net income of $110.8M in 2024, driven by significant impairment charges related to Indian Motorcycle and goodwill write-downs.
kpis.signal: Substantial net loss in 2025 versus $110.8M net income in 2024.

kpis.name: Research and Development
kpis.explanation: Expenditures dedicated to innovation and development of new products and technologies.
kpis.description: R&D spending increased 10% in 2025, rising from $336.9M in 2024 to $371.9M in 2025, reflecting continued commitment to product innovation and technology.
kpis.signal: R&D investment growth despite margin pressure, reflecting ongoing innovation commitment.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating income divided by revenue, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Operating margin was negative at -4.9% in 2025 versus +4.0% in 2024, driven by exceptional charges (Indian Motorcycle impairment of $330.4M, goodwill impairment of $52.6M) and tariff pressure.
kpis.signal: Shift to operating loss in 2025 due to impairments and exceptional charges.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $7.152B in most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -$0.466B in most recent fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Worldwide ORV Sales
kpis.explanation: Total number of off-road vehicles (ATVs and side-by-sides) sold at retail globally.
kpis.description: Worldwide ORV sales reached 970,000 units in 2025, up 2.6% from 945,000 units in 2024, marking a recovery following modest prior declines.
kpis.signal: Global ORV market recovery in 2025 with 2.6% growth following 2024 decline.

kpis.name: North America ORV Sales
kpis.explanation: Number of off-road vehicles (ATVs and side-by-sides) sold at retail in North America.
kpis.description: North America ORV sales reached 780,000 units in 2025, up slightly 0.6% versus 775,000 in 2024, marking stabilization after a 55,000 unit decline between 2023 and 2024.
kpis.signal: North American market stabilization after two years of decline, with modest growth.

risks.title: Sensitivity to general economic conditions
risks.score_rationale: This risk is highlighted in the 10-K as having already affected the company and capable of significantly impacting demand. Language is repetitive and emphasizes direct impact on sales and profitability. Macro category is heavily weighted in inflationary context. Existential risk in case of sustained recession.

risks.title: Increases in raw material and freight costs
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned early in the document, with explicit references to past and future inflationary pressures. Direct impact on gross margin is clear. Text underscores persistent supply chain and energy cost challenges. Industrial category is highly impactful.

risks.title: Regulatory restrictions on PFAS
risks.score_rationale: Risk is described with concerned language (non-availability, adversely impact). Affects supply chain and competitiveness. While new or reinforced, still in regulatory evolution phase. Regulation category is moderately weighted but risk is strategically significant.

risks.title: Impact of tariffs and trade measures
risks.score_rationale: Risk is well-developed with mention of concrete cost and competitiveness effects. Text notes elevated uncertainty and rapidly evolving environment. Impact is combined with inflation, amplifying the risk. Geopolitical category is currently heavily weighted.

risks.title: Increased competition across all markets
risks.score_rationale: Risk is extensively detailed with mention of better-funded, more innovative, or better-positioned geographic competitors. Language is concerned (failure to compete could negatively impact). Competition category is critical for discretionary consumer goods player.

risks.title: Dependence on innovation and product development
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes need for heavy R&D investments and speed against competitors. Explicit mention of electrification and artificial intelligence. Risk is strategically important for the future. Technology category is increasing in importance.

risks.title: Risks related to strategic transactions and Indian Motorcycle separation
risks.score_rationale: Risk is detailed with concrete examples (Indian Motorcycle separation). Text mentions unforeseen costs, operational disruptions, and integration failure risk. Capital category is relevant as it relates to growth strategy.

risks.title: Supply chain disruptions
risks.score_rationale: Risk is described as capable of causing complete production suspension. Mention of single sources, logistical delays, and geopolitical risks. Strong language (suspend production entirely). Direct impact on revenues. Industrial category is critical.

ai_positioning.summary: PII does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
